properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued November 25 at 9:12PM EST until November 25 at 10:00PM EST by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
SMWKEY

The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Hawk Channel and Straits of Florida from Ocean Reef to Craig Key
out 20 nm...

* Until 1000 PM EST.

* At 912 PM EST, a strong thunderstorm was located over Islamorada
Hump, moving northeast at 35 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly higher
waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.

* Locations in the warning include...
Key Largo Dry Rocks, Mosquito Bank Light, South Rips, Islamorada
Hump, French Ref, Spiegel Grove, and Grecian Rocks.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, steep and fast-building
seas, frequent lightning, and blinding downpours. Stay low or go
below, and make sure all on board are wearing life jackets.

Intense and continuous lightning is occurring with this storm. Stay
low, or go below. Lower VHF antenna, outriggers, fishing rods, and
umbrellas.
properties.area: Hawk Channel from Ocean Reef to Craig Key out to the reef; Straits of Florida from Ocean Reef to Craig Key out 20 NM

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued November 25 at 8:56PM EST until November 25 at 11:15PM EST by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southwestern Carteret County in eastern North Carolina...
Southeastern Craven County in eastern North Carolina...
Southeastern Jones County in eastern North Carolina...
Onslow County in eastern North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 1115 PM EST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 855 PM EST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain. Minor flooding
is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory area.
Between 2 and 4 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Jacksonville, Havelock, Morehead City, Newport, Harkers Island,
Piney Green, Camp Lejeune Center, Pumpkin Center, New River
Station, Stella, Swansboro, Hubert, Cape Carteret, North River,
Straits, Smyrna, Marshallberg, Pine Knoll Shores, Harlowe and
Silverdale.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.
properties.area: Carteret, NC; Craven, NC; Jones, NC; Onslow, NC

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 25 at 8:32PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Previous rainfall working through the basin will cause river levels
on the St. Johns at Deland to continue rising through Major Flood
Stage. The river is forecast to rise above its former record crest
this weekend, reaching 6.4 feet, where it is expected to linger into
early next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 5.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Wednesday was 5.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise through Major Flood
Stage, reaching 6.4 feet late this weekend. The river is then
forecast to remain steady through early next week.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday afternoon at noon EST.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 25 at 2:17PM PST until November 27 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rain over the Olympics overnight plus an additional 2-4 inches
of rain, with snow levels well above mountain tops, will drive the
Skokomish River above flood stage this evening to above Moderate
flood.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM PST Wednesday the stage was 16.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 17.9 feet late tomorrow
morning. It will then fall below flood stage late Friday morning.
Further rises through the weekend are likely, with exceeding
flood stage possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 25 at 10:33AM PST until November 26 at 6:00PM PST by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides.

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the Sacramento River, San Joaquin
River, and other Delta waterways in Solano, Yolo, Sacramento, and
San Joaquin Counties.


* WHEN...Until 600 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 944 AM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides each day are forecast as follows (all times
local). MHHW is Mean Higher High Water, or the average
highest daily tide; MLLW is Mean Lower Low Water, or the
average lowest daily tide.
* Port Chicago: +2.6 ft MHHW (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:01 PM Wed
11/25, +2.5 ft MHHW (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:51 PM Thu 11/26, +2.2
ft MHHW (7.1 ft MLLW) at 2:45 PM Fri 11/27, and +1.7 ft MHHW
(6.6 ft MLLW) at 3:44 PM Sat 11/28.
* West Sacramento: +2.4 ft MHHW (6.8 ft MLLW) at 4:18 PM Wed
11/25, +2.3 ft MHHW (6.7 ft MLLW) at 5:08 PM Thu 11/26, +2.1
ft MHHW (6.5 ft MLLW) at 6:02 PM Fri 11/27, and +1.8 ft MHHW
(6.2 ft MLLW) at 6:59 PM Sat 11/28.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.5 ft at 3:00 PM Wed 11/25,
+7.4 ft at 4:00 PM Thu 11/26, +7.3 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/27,
+6.9 ft at 6:00 PM Sat 11/28 and +6.2 ft at 7:00 PM Sun
11/29.
- These predictions include up to +1.5 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.
- Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at:
* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144
* West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide
predictions.html?id=9416131
* Rio Vista: https://water.noaa.gov/gauges/RVBC1
properties.instruction:
Some roads that are commonly dry may become inundated during high
tide. If you encounter flooded roadways: turn around, dont drown.
properties.area: Sacramento, CA; San Joaquin, CA; Solano, CA; Yolo, CA
